slides.0.title: Macedonia and Thessaly
slides.0.subtitle: Naoussa and the red heartland of the north
slides.1.title: Three Xinomavro appellations: Naoussa, Amyndeo, Goumenissa
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Naoussa
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Red only, 100% Xinomavro; limestone clay and marl; oak ageing required; the northern flagship PDO
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Amyndeo (Amyntaio)
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Xinomavro only; dry, semi-dry and semi-sweet reds and rosés plus sparkling rosé; a cooler, higher site with sandy and clay soils
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Goumenissa
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Dry red, Xinomavro blended with Negoska (at least 20%); vineyards must lie above 150 m; Negoska makes it softer than Naoussa
slides.1.content: Mnemonic: Naoussa = structure and ageing; Amyndeo = coolness and sparkling rosé; Goumenissa = Negoska-softened.
slides.2.title: Xinomavro: altitude and style
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Moderate altitude
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Dry reds with good colour and acidity, high alcohol and rich tannin; ageworthy
slides.2.highlights.1.title: High altitude
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Can make rosé, sparkling and even blanc de noirs, with red-berry and strawberry aromas
slides.2.highlights.2.title: One grape, many faces
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Altitude, soil and winemaking shape style: ideal Diploma essay material
slides.2.content: In essays, contrast Naoussa (structure) with Amyndeo (coolness) to show one grape's range.
slides.3.title: Slopes of Meliton: whites and reds of Halkidiki
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Location
slides.3.highlights.0.content: On the Halkidiki peninsula in south-eastern Macedonia, close to the sea
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Whites
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Dry whites from Assyrtiko, Athiri and Roditis
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Reds
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Led by Limnio with Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc
slides.3.content: One of the few northern PDOs with both reds and whites and international grapes; its style differs from the Xinomavro areas.
slides.4.title: Thessaly: Rapsani, Messenikola, Anchialos
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Rapsani
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Dry red blending Xinomavro, Stavroto and Krassato; schist soils
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Messenikola
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Dry red, at least 70% Mavro Messenikola with Carignan and Syrah
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Anchialos
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Dry white, at least 80% Roditis, the balance Savatiano
slides.4.content: A memory aid for Thessaly's three PDOs: Rapsani = blended red, Messenikola = red with French grapes, Anchialos = white.
slides.5.componentProps.slide.title: 🧠 Knowledge Check
Which grape is blended with Xinomavro in Goumenissa?
Negoska makes Goumenissa softer than Naoussa.
Which PDO allows a naturally sparkling rosé?
Amyndeo is known for its cool altitude and sparkling rosé.
What kind of wine is Anchialos?
A. A dry white led by Roditis
Anchialos is a dry white of at least 80% Roditis in Thessaly.
